This is a difficult game for me to review, because I don’t think it’s a bad game at all. In fact, in many ways, it’s clearly a very clever one.

The whole idea is fascinating: you design circuits, place components on a board, program tiny chips, and make them communicate with each other to solve increasingly complex problems. It has that typical Zachtronics feeling of being elegant, nerdy, and extremely satisfying when everything finally works.

And when the game clicks, it really does feel great. Finding a solution, watching the signals move through your little system, and realizing that your messy pile of instructions actually works — that can be genuinely rewarding.

But for me, this was also where the problem started.

Compared to other games from the same developer, this one felt much more tiring than fun. The concepts never became fully intuitive to me. The difference between buses, pins, chip communication, timing, and all the small technical rules often felt more like something I had to study than something I naturally understood through play.

Yes, the game includes a big manual, and yes, that is part of the charm. But at some point I had to ask myself: am I playing a game, or am I doing homework?

The optimization also didn’t hook me the way it did in other Zachtronics games. Instead of wanting to improve my solutions, I often just wanted to be done with them. Near the end, I was finishing the game more out of obligation than enjoyment, and I even started looking up solutions online — which, for a puzzle game, is usually a sign that something has stopped working for me.

So I respect this game a lot. I admire its design, its theme, and its ambition. For the right kind of player, especially someone who enjoys programming, electronics, or very technical puzzle games, this might be fantastic.

But for me, it became too exhausting. It felt more impressive than enjoyable.

So even though I can see why people love it, I personally can’t recommend it. Not because it’s poorly made, but because the experience just wasn’t fun enough for me to justify a positive review.

先进行整体评价：必然是好评！
这款游戏让我对嵌入式开发和汇编语言有了一个初步的认识，同时需要进行思考才能解答出题目。你的解答不一定是最优解，需要利用逻辑电路、数模转换器等等元件进行电路的简化。当解答出问题的时候，你可以与所有解答出问题的人进行代码量、消耗电力和总价格数的比较，从而思考自己的解答是否存在更优解。同时还有纸牌，如果累了可以玩纸牌放松一下
下面是针对不同类型玩家的推荐程度：（满分5星）
1. 计算机科学、自动化相关专业，尤其是希望入门嵌入式开发的玩家：5星。该游戏的元件同时含有数电与模电的元件，还有可编程的元件，同时简化了大量的连线操作，每个元件都只有几个接口，对于想要知道嵌入式开发相关概念并体验是非常容易的
2. 希望系统提升嵌入式开发能力的玩家：3星。该游戏对于嵌入式开发有些过于简单，且目前的嵌入式开发更多的使用的是C语言（本人对于嵌入式开发了解得不够深，这是主观感受，如有不当欢迎批评指正），即使是嵌入式汇编开发，该汇编语言也过于简单，相较于常规的汇编语言简化了大量的概念，比如立即数、寻址相关，日常放松娱乐尚可
3. 学习过《计算机组成原理》《汇编语言程序设计》或者玩过《Turing Complete》（需要达到设计汇编指令，甚至用自己的汇编指令写过代码的地步）这款游戏的玩家：5星。你有了汇编语言与数字电路的基础知识，当你在阅读文档、学习汇编代码的时候会比没有任何基础的人轻松许多，同时你有过数字电路的基础，其中元件的逻辑门符号一眼就能看懂，数模转换器也很容易上手
4. 把该游戏当成单纯的解谜游戏，只是抱着试一试的心态上手的玩家：1星。赶紧跑！这个游戏有一定的专业壁垒，并且非常烧脑，不适合你们！
